The patch reverts __hash__ to hash(self.creation_counter), which is immutable and matches the upstream Django fix. The patch reverts __hash__ to hash(self.creation_counter), which is what the issue proposes and matches the upstream Django fix. __eq__ still compares the model as well, so equal fields still hash equally and fields that share a creation_counter across abstract-model inheritance are still told apart by equality. Hash immutability is restored.

The patch fixes the logic so that passed symbols are used and the default is used only when none are given. The upstream fix is nearly identical. The only change to the error message wording is a risk if a hidden test matches the text, but tests most likely check only for ValueError.

The upstream fix adds set_paths that sets self._paths and also sets self.stale = True. This patch sets self._paths but omits the stale flag, so the artist won't be marked for redraw. The patch adds Choices.__str__ returning str(self.value), which matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #30902). Because TextChoices(str, Choices) and IntegerChoices(int, Choices) have Choices after the mixin in the MRO, Choices.__str__ is found before str.__str__ or int.__str__ and is used. The patch fixes the bug: if symbols are given with the correct count, they are used; if none are given, ring.symbols is used; a wrong count still raises ValueError. The edge case of an empty ring (ngens=0) is handled because symbols is empty and falls back to ring.symbols, which is also empty.

The core set_paths method matches the upstream fix, setting _paths and invalidating the old-style split collections. The patch removes the forced zero dash offset in Patch.draw, so the offset in _dash_pattern is now passed through to the renderer. This matches the upstream fix, which removed that override. The patch handles an empty ast.Tuple in both the Python domain's annotation unparser and pycode.ast.unparse, returning '()' instead of popping from an empty list. The patch adds a special case in Set.intersect for Reals that assumes self.args[0].args is an expression list, which holds only for ImageSet (self.args[0] is a Lambda). For any other set (Interval, FiniteSet, Union), it either raises errors or returns wrong results. It also references a `Reals` name that is probably not imported in sets.py. The core change removes the offset-zeroing in Patch.draw, which matches the upstream fix for this issue. The patch also adds stray files (reproduce_error.py, test_edge_cases.py) at the repo root. The patch overrides world_to_pixel in HighLevelWCSWrapper, but it does not fix the bug, which is in SlicedLowLevelWCS.world_to_pixel_values (dropped world dimensions filled with 1.0 instead of the value at the slice). The override also breaks the wrapper: it bypasses the high-level conversion of SkyCoord/Quantity objects into low-level values, and it compares the number of high-level objects against world_n_dim, which fails since one SkyCoord covers two dims. SlicedLowLevelWCS is not imported, and _apply_slicing_pixel_transform doesn't exist, so it would raise a NameError or AttributeError.

The patch preserves list/tuple type via type(value)(generator), and recursion handles expression items (including F with simple_col). Problem: type(value)(generator) breaks for namedtuples, which take positional args rather than an iterable. The upstream Django fix at this time was `type(value)(generator)` too, and namedtuple handling was added later (#30739 follow-up). The recursion into resolve_lookup_value handles F and expressions as before: the top-level branch checks hasattr resolve_expression, and F gets simple_col. Behavior matches the upstream fix.

The patch matches the upstream astropy fix. It replaces the hard-coded world value 1.0 for sliced-out world dimensions with the world coordinate at the slice position, computed via the existing _pixel_to_world_values_all helper.

The patch changes coordinate merging to always use combine_attrs="override" for every apply_ufunc call, which alters existing behavior (e.g. keep_attrs=False or 'drop' previously dropped coordinate attrs via merge). It also adds a post-hoc loop that overwrites coordinate attrs, which is hacky and may break existing tests. The real upstream fix was just to pass keep_attrs=True/lambda handling in where. Also `da.coords.items()` yields DataArrays, and setting `coord_var.attrs` on those may not modify the underlying variable (for index coords it may copy), so the restoration may not even work. Risk of breaking hidden tests such as keep_attrs=False cases where coord attrs are expected to be dropped is high.

The patch fixes the inverted logic in as_expr: given symbols of the right count are now kept, a wrong count still raises ValueError, and no symbols falls back to ring.symbols. This matches the upstream fix. The stray reproduce.py and test_edge_cases.py files are clutter but should not affect hidden tests.

The patch adds refit_time_ measured around the refit step, which matches the upstream fix (which also uses time.time()). The extra reproduce.py file is clutter but harmless. The attribute is only set when refit is truthy, matching upstream. Hidden tests check that refit_time_ exists and is a float, which this satisfies.

The upstream fix added `__str__` to the `Choices` base class so that IntegerChoices and TextChoices both return `str(self.value)`. This patch only adds `__str__` to TextChoices, so IntegerChoices still returns 'IntegerChoices.X' from str(). The issue title names both types, and hidden tests likely check IntegerChoices str() too (e.g. test_str in enums tests iterates over Suit/YearInSchool/Vehicle). It also adds a stray reproduce.py file to the repo root. The CharField changes are extra but harmless. Since the upstream test includes `self.assertEqual(str(Suit.DIAMOND), '1')`, the patch would fail it.

The fix computes the dropped world coordinate by calling pixel_to_world_values with zeros for all other pixel axes. That is wrong for a coupled PC matrix, because the world value of the dropped axis depends on the other pixel coordinates, so the result is only correct when those are 0. In the issue's WCS, wavelength depends on pixel axes 1, 2 and 3 through PC3_2=-1, so the value computed at pixel (0,0,0) differs from the true value at the sliced pixel. The upstream fix uses world_to_pixel at the pixel-slice position for the whole coordinate, not zeros. Also, `numbers` may not be imported in the file. It was imported for _slices_pixel handling? Unclear. The new ValueError on the number of world arguments could break existing callers. The patch also modifies pyproject.toml and adds stray scripts, which is bad hygiene. Overall it likely fails the hidden test, which checks the result for a coupled WCS.

The patch moves set_paths into the base Collection, so ContourSet (a Collection subclass) inherits it. However, the upstream fix added ContourSet.set_paths and changed ContourSet's internals. In this version, ContourSet may store paths via self._paths, with get_paths returning self._paths, so setting self._paths works; the collection base implementation sets _paths and marks stale. Other subclasses that previously raised NotImplementedError (PolyCollection, LineCollection, QuadMesh, etc.) now silently accept paths, which could break hidden tests expecting NotImplementedError, but that is unlikely to be tested. Upstream fix (PR #25020?) did: Collection.set_paths raises NotImplementedError still; ContourSet.set_paths sets self._paths = paths and stale. Hidden test likely test_contour_set_paths or similar, calling cs.set_paths and checking get_paths. Here ContourSet inherits the base, which works if ContourSet.get_paths returns self._paths. In this matplotlib version ContourSet.__init__ sets self._paths via the collection init, so it should work. Risk: PathCollection set_paths removed but inherited, fine. Subclasses like QuadMesh or _CollectionWithSizes may have their own override, so fine. Likely passes.

The patch removes the zeroing of the dash offset in Patch.draw, so offsets now take effect, which matches the upstream fix. The leftover _setattr_cm with the same value is a harmless no-op. Existing tests that relied on the ignored offset could break, but the upstream fix made the same change, so those tests were presumably updated.

The patch matches the upstream sympy fix: it intersects the base set with the solutions of the numerator of the imaginary part, then subtracts the denominator zeros, using a helper that falls back to a ConditionSet. Concerns are an unused or circular import of numer, and ConditionSet(sym, Eq(i,0)) lacking a base set, which is probably fine. The fix itself looks correct.

The patch checks `name in merged_indexes` before `merged_indexes[name] = index` is assigned, so it is almost always False at that point and the else branch runs, unchanged from the old behavior. The bug is not fixed. Even if the branch did run, it would prepend the variable's own attrs to the merge list, which could change combine_attrs semantics. The real fix was in `where`/`apply_ufunc`, using a keep_attrs callable that handles coordinates (attrs[1] only for the data variable). So this patch fails the issue.

The patch adds refit_time_ measured around the best estimator's refit, which is what the issue asks for and matches the upstream fix (which uses time.time() and sets refit_time_ only when refit is true). The local `import time` is stylistically poor but works. The docs are missing, but hidden tests only check that the attribute exists and is a float.

The core change in django/utils/html.py matches the upstream Django fix: it imports html and returns mark_safe(html.escape(str(text))). Removing _html_escapes is safe unless other code uses it; upstream removed it too. The ' to ' change is expected by the updated hidden tests. The stray benchmark.py and test_escape.py files at the repo root are clutter but do not affect the tests.

The patch adds time import, times the refit of best_estimator_, and stores refit_time_ only when refit is set, matching the upstream scikit-learn fix. Hidden tests check that refit_time_ exists and is a float when refit is True, and is absent otherwise, which this satisfies.

The resolver is far too broad: is_literal_value returns True for any alphabetic string, so any unresolved class like 'Foo' or 'MyMissingClass' is silently accepted and nitpick warnings are suppressed. Existing tests that expect nitpick warnings for missing references would likely fail. The patch also pollutes the repo with build artifacts, test scripts, and unrelated setup.py dependency pins, and it does not properly handle Literal in the annotation parser, which is the real upstream fix.

The patch only avoids the IndexError, so `Tuple[()]` renders as `Tuple[]` and the empty tuple's parentheses are lost. The upstream fix emits `(` and `)` punctuation nodes for an empty tuple, and the hidden test most likely expects them, so this patch would fail it.

The patch rewrites the Reals branch of ImageSet intersection and changes semantics. It was not reasoned through fully; several problems are likely. The original code computed base_set minus the zeros of the imaginary part, which is wrong in general, but the upstream fix was different, intersecting with the solutions where im==0. Here, solveset(im, n, S.Integers) for (n-1)(n+1) gives {-1, 1}, the intersection works, and it returns {-1, 1}, which matches the issue. However, the new code is over-broad: it replaces the original 'base_set - zeros' logic with a result containing only the zeros, which is correct, but the fallback for non-finite solutions retains the old, buggy behavior. For example, when the imaginary part is zero for no integers (solveset returns EmptySet), it is not a FiniteSet, so it falls to the old path with zip(*[]) possibly failing. Also, in the FiniteSet path the denominators are ignored, so a value making a denominator zero can be returned. The re.subs may also include unevaluated results. Also, the elif/else structure: the code before the else branch, where im is a constant and other cases, may fall through to None, because the final return was moved inside the else. A path that previously reached 'return imageset(lam, base_set)', such as the im==0 branch, now returns None. That is a regression. The hidden tests likely include other cases, so this is risky.

The patch changes _af_new to a classmethod, but the module-level alias `_af_new = Permutation._af_new` remains bound to Permutation, so internal calls still work. However, __new__ and other methods use the `_af_new` function or `Perm`, so subclass instances created via Permutation.__new__ would still be Permutation. The upstream fix changed many call sites (e.g. __new__ uses cls._af_new, and methods use self._af_new). This patch alone does not make subclassing work, and hidden tests likely check a subclass (e.g. a Permutation subclass's operations returning the subclass). Those tests would fail.

The patch closely matches the upstream xarray fix, which restores coord attrs by rebuilding attrs from x after apply_ufunc. Note the upstream fix passes keep_attrs=True through to apply_ufunc, whereas this patch also does so (keep_attrs remains True), so merge behavior is consistent. Edge cases such as x being a scalar are handled via getattr defaults. The Dataset/non-Dataset special case and coord loop match upstream.

The rewrite is not a valid HNF algorithm: it uses row operations and zeroes entries to the right of pivots, which discards the column-operation semantics (the column space/lattice is not preserved). It also has a convoluted pivot-finding loop with dubious logic, returns a full m x n matrix, and would break the existing HNF tests, which expect column-style output with a different shape. The patch also adds a stray reproduction script to the repo root.

The patch defines __str__ on Choices, but TextChoices(str, Choices) and IntegerChoices(int, Choices) have MRO [TextChoices, str, Choices, Enum, object], so str.__str__ would be found before Choices.__str__. However, the actual upstream fix put __str__ in Choices and it worked. With a str mixin, Python's enum machinery: str.__str__ exists on str, and MRO would pick str's __str__ first, returning the value anyway... but for the issue the output was 'MyChoice.FIRST_CHOICE', which means Enum.__str__ was used. EnumMeta replaces __str__ in the class dict for mixed-in types only in certain cases (Python 3.8-3.10 in __new__ it sets __reduce_ex__ only). The observed behavior shows Enum.__str__ used, so the MRO must be [IntegerChoices, int, Choices, Enum]; int defines __repr__ but not __str__ (object.__str__ is inherited, not in int's dict), so lookup goes to Choices.__str__ before reaching object. For str, str does define __str__ in its own dict, so TextChoices(str, Choices) would pick str.__str__, which returns the raw string for a str subclass... that would give 'first' already, contradicting the issue. Actually the issue shows Enum.__str__ was used, so Enum's metaclass must override it; in Python 3.11+ it differs, but Django at that time ran on 3.6-3.8. Upstream fix is identical (def __str__(self): return str(self.value) in Choices), so the patch matches upstream. The trailing whitespace line is harmless.

The patch breaks the base object construction: `super(Permutation, cls).__new__(cls)` resolves to `Basic.__new__(cls)` with no args, so `_args` is empty; previously `Basic.__new__(Perm, perm)` stored perm as args. This affects hash, equality (`_hashable_content` is overridden, but `args` is used elsewhere, e.g. in copy/pickle/free_symbols). Also `p.__init__()` is called in `_af_new`, and `Permutation.__new__` returns an instance so Python calls `__init__(*args)` again, which is a double init and fails for subclasses whose `__init__` takes no args. Most importantly, only `__mul__` and `__invert__` were updated; many other methods (`__pow__`, `rank`, `next_lex`, etc.) still call `_af_new(perm)` with the default class and return plain `Permutation`. `_af_new` as a module-level alias is called with `cls` as the second argument, so existing callers like `Perm._af_new` are mostly unaffected, but the subclassing fix is incomplete and `args` loss could break existing tests (e.g. `Permutation.args`, `sympify`/`srepr`).

This matches the upstream Django change (ticket #30...): escape() now uses html.escape, and urlize's custom unescape is replaced by html.unescape. Upstream did exactly this, and the tests were updated to expect '. html.unescape handles a superset of entities, and the upstream commit made the same replacement in trim_punctuation and the url handling. Behavior for the hidden tests should match.

The patch adds a check `if not name: raise ValueError(...)` before the dot check, which matches the upstream Flask fix. The only other diff is the last line `return f`, which looks like a whitespace or newline-at-EOF change and has no behavioral effect. Existing tests that create blueprints with non-empty names are unaffected.

The core change in Blueprint.__init__ raises ValueError for empty or whitespace-only names, which satisfies the issue; the upstream fix is `if not name: raise ValueError(...)`. Hidden tests likely check `Blueprint('', __name__)` raises ValueError, which passes. The stray reproduce.py and test_edge_cases.py files are clutter, but they are not collected by pytest (test_edge_cases.py is at the repo root and would run module-level code only if collected, and it passes without error). Rejecting whitespace-only names is slightly stricter than upstream but unlikely to break existing tests.

The patch calls html.escape but the diff does not show an import of the stdlib html module in django/utils/html.py. The module is itself named html but is inside the django.utils package, so absolute import is fine, yet without 'import html' (or 'from html import escape as html_escape') this raises NameError. The original file's imports are not shown in the diff, and the upstream Django fix added 'from html import escape' in the import section. The patch leaves _html_escapes unused and, since it doesn't add an import, escape() would likely fail with NameError at runtime. Also, existing tests expecting ' would need updating, though hidden tests will cover the new ' output.

The patch adds an empty-name check in Blueprint.__init__ that raises ValueError, matching the issue and the upstream Flask fix. The check comes after super().__init__, which is harmless and consistent with the existing dot check. Existing tests should be unaffected, since valid blueprints always have non-empty names.

The upstream fix handled Literal in the Python domain's type-annotation parser (sphinx/domains/python.py, _parse_annotation), where `Literal[...]` args are turned into cross-references. This patch only changes restify/stringify in util/typing.py. stringify output is parsed by _parse_annotation, so ':const:`True`' would be tokenized into odd pieces (punctuation, names), likely still producing py:class xrefs for 'const' or 'True' and broken display. It also changes existing outputs that tests compare (e.g. stringify(Literal[1]) expected 'Literal[1]'), so existing tests would fail.

The patch registers '--skip-checks' four times in add_arguments. argparse raises ArgumentError ('conflicting option string: --skip-checks') on duplicate registration, so the runserver command would fail to parse arguments at all. Every runserver invocation and test would break.

The patch replaces global `_af_new` and `Perm` uses with `cls`/`self` equivalents. It matches the upstream sympy fix (PR #15412 style), where `__new__` ends with `cls._af_new(aform)`, and `_af_new` becomes a classmethod. Existing callers of `Permutation._af_new(perm)` and `_af_new = Perm._af_new` still work with a classmethod. `isinstance(a, cls)` in `__new__` changes behaviour only for subclasses, and plain Permutation is unaffected. The size handling that `__new__` previously did (`size = len(aform)`) is now done in `_af_new` via `len(perm)`, so it is equivalent. The `__new__` path with `size` and a Permutation argument: `cls(a.array_form, size=size)` is fine. Remaining module-level uses of `_af_new` exist elsewhere, but they still work for the base class. Overall this is the same as the upstream fix and should pass the tests.

The patch only flips the default of check_rank to True in the public function; it does not fix the HNF algorithm that drops rows. With check_rank=True, _hnf raises DMShapeError if rank is less than the number of rows, which is a behavior change. Also, the actual bug is in _hermite_normal_form, which removes rows when the matrix has fewer pivots than columns, and this patch leaves that untouched. The issue's matrix is 3x2 after the transpose and flips, with rank 2, and the algorithm would still drop the zero columns incorrectly. The real fix changes the algorithm so that it does not remove rows or columns when the pivot position is zero. Also, the diff touches the final line without a change, which looks like a newline-only edit.

The patch changes the cache key to use str(lang) instead of format_type, which is wrong: the issue is that format_type may be a lazy string, and the failure is in getattr(settings, format_type). The patch does not convert format_type to str, so the TypeError still occurs for lazy strings. It also modifies the wrong element of the cache key.

The `hasattr(format_type, '__str__')` check is true for every object in Python 3, so `str()` is applied unconditionally. Lazy strings now convert correctly, which fixes the issue. The upstream fix is `format_type = str(format_type)`, so the behavior is essentially the same. `get_format(None)` would now look up 'None' instead of raising, but that is an edge case that hidden tests are unlikely to cover. The stray reproduce.py file is clutter but harmless.

The patch converts format_type to str before it is used as a cache key and in getattr, which fixes the lazy-string TypeError. It matches the upstream Django fix, and str() on a plain string is a harmless no-op.

This matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #31... temporal subtraction without ExpressionWrapper): moves the DurationExpression/TemporalSubtraction detection into resolve_expression, and DurationExpression.as_sql delegates to super when the DB has a native duration field. The upstream fix is nearly identical, including the isinstance guard and the AttributeError catch. One concern is that TemporalSubtraction is a subclass of SQLiteNumericMixin/CombinedExpression with its own as_sql, which is fine. The isinstance guard avoids recursion. Looks correct.

The core change adds cls._clear_cached_lookups() to _unregister_lookup, matching the upstream fix and the behavior of register_lookup. The extra reproduce.py file at the repo root is clutter but does not affect tests. The schema test change from the issue is test-only, and the hidden tests should pass with this fix.

The patch only loosens the as_sql check so that mixed datetime types (e.g. DateField - DateTimeField) take the TemporalSubtraction path. It does not touch output_field resolution, which is where the issue's FieldError originates: F('end') - F('start') is a CombinedExpression whose _resolve_output_field sees DateTimeField and DateTimeField and raises no error, but the result type is still DateTimeField, not Duration. Adding Value(timedelta, DurationField) then makes the outer expression mixed (DateTimeField vs DurationField) and raises the error. The real fix adds a _resolve_output_field in CombinedExpression, or registers combinators such as (DateTimeField, DateTimeField, SUB) -> DurationField in _connector_combinators. This patch does not resolve the issue, and it can also change as_sql behavior for mismatched types.

The upstream fix adds the same '--skip-checks' argument in runserver and wraps the checks in 'if not options['skip_checks']'. BaseCommand.execute handles skip_checks by itself only if requires_system_checks and not options.get('skip_checks'); runserver sets requires_system_checks=False, so no conflict. Tests calling inner_run with options lacking skip_checks could KeyError, but the upstream fix uses the same options['skip_checks'] access, so it matches. The argument is a store_true with dest skip_checks, which is fine.

The patch adds cls._clear_cached_lookups() to _unregister_lookup, mirroring register_lookup. In Django's actual fix, the same single line was added (the upstream commit also updated tests). The method _clear_cached_lookups exists as a classmethod in this version, as register_lookup uses it. The change is correct and minimal.

The patch matches the upstream Sphinx fix: constants are rendered with repr, Text nodes inside Literal[...] are wrapped in nodes.literal, and those nodes are unwrapped without a cross-reference in _parse_annotation, so nitpick no longer flags them.

The patch sets requires_system_checks = '__all__' on runserver, so BaseCommand.execute runs checks once up front, and then inner_run checks again. This causes double checks on every start, and checks run before the autoreloader forks, which defeats the purpose of the comment that validation happens on each reload. The upstream fix keeps requires_system_checks = [] and uses 'skip_checks' with parser default True in add_arguments. Here, with '__all__', --skip-checks is a base option so it skips the execute checks, but options.get('skip_checks') in inner_run: without the flag, options['skip_checks'] is False by default, fine. But upstream sets default skip_checks True in handle for runserver via options; here the base behavior differs: checks run twice. Hidden tests likely check that checks are called only once or that skip_checks passes through to the inner_run, e.g. mock check not called when --skip-checks. Also the patch adds a stray test_runserver.py file and modifies tests/test_sqlite.py with DEBUG = True, which pollutes the repo and could break tests relying on DEBUG=False defaults. Double checks may break existing tests such as asserting check called once (test_runserver_addrport etc.). Overall defective.

The patch iterates over all rows from the bottom and breaks once k reaches 0, so a row with no pivot no longer uses up the min(m, n) limit. This matches the upstream sympy fix and handles the issue's case.

The patch only makes _aggregate_score_dicts tolerate an empty list, which hides the IndexError. The real bug is that a generator of splits gets consumed on the first candidate evaluation, so later cross_val_score calls get empty splits. The upstream fix calls check_cv and list(cv.split(...)) in SequentialFeatureSelector.fit. With this patch, the user's example would likely fail differently or silently: later calls return empty results and np.mean of an empty array gives nan, so the selection becomes wrong. Hidden tests that pass splits would fail.

The core fix sets the pk attribute to None after fast delete, matching the upstream Django fix (setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None) inside the fast-delete branch). The extra reproduce.py file at repo root is clutter, but it is not a test and not imported, so it doesn't affect hidden tests.

This matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #30931): it only sets get_FOO_display when the class doesn't already define it. Model inheritance could in principle be affected, since a parent's get_FOO_display would be inherited and block the child's field from overriding it. Upstream accepted this same approach, and the related tests pass.

The patch calls check_cv once in fit, which turns the splits iterable into a reusable CV splitter (_CVIterableWrapper, which stores the list of splits). This matches the upstream fix. The same cv object is then reused across every cross_val_score call, so the generator is no longer exhausted. Passing y into check_cv is correct, and is_classifier is imported properly. The signature change to _get_best_new_feature_score is only called internally.

The patch makes _get_FIELD_display look up get_<attname>_display on self, but that attribute is the partialmethod set by contribute_to_class, which calls _get_FIELD_display. This causes infinite recursion for every model with choices that doesn't override the method. When overridden, the override is called directly and never reaches here, so the added code is useless. The real fix is in contribute_to_class, which should only set the method if the class doesn't already define it.

The patch only modifies IndexColumns and leaves Columns.__str__ untouched, so the "name"DESC case from the issue is not fixed. It also removes the IndexError guard in IndexColumns.col_str, and self.col_suffixes[idx] can raise IndexError if col_suffixes is shorter than columns. IndexColumns is created with col_suffixes=() by default in some paths (e.g. _create_index_sql with no suffixes), so a missing suffix list would crash. The upstream fix changed Columns to use '{} {}'.format and kept a try/except in IndexColumns, so this patch is incomplete and unsafe.

The patch adds cls._clear_cached_lookups() after deleting the lookup in _unregister_lookup, mirroring register_lookup, which is what the issue asks for. _clear_cached_lookups exists in this Django version and is a classmethod that clears the cache on the class and its subclasses. The upstream fix is the same one-line change, and the test changes are not needed for correctness.

The patch changes _resolve_output_field to special-case temporal ops, but the nested expression in the issue, (F('end') - F('start')) + Value(duration), has sources [DateTimeField (from the inner CombinedExpression's own resolved output_field), DurationField]. The inner expression's output_field would resolve via the same method to DurationField since both sources are DateTimeField, giving DurationField + DurationField, which passes. So the issue case likely works. However, the patch adds stray files (reproduce.py, test_app, test_settings.py) to the repo root, which pollutes it. The case 2 branch returns the temporal source field for datetime + duration, which is right. The real upstream fix added a _resolve_output_field in CombinedExpression and handled the DurationField/mixed cases there, and the edit here to BaseExpression changes behaviour for all expressions with a 'connector' attribute, e.g. Q objects aren't affected but other things might be. The case 1 check applies to any expression with 2 sources, including DateField - DateField from a Func? Only those with connector. Also the as_sql change uses hasattr(self,'output_field'), which triggers the property and might raise FieldError for mixed types, a regression risk. Also the sources[0].get_internal_type() with 2 sources only; the mixed-type error case with non-temporal remains. Stray files like test_app/models.py could break the test suite (e.g. app label conflicts). Overall risky.

The patch maps an inverted generator r[i] to domain.generators[k]**-1, but images is keyed by the generators only, so `s in images` is False for the inverted s and the term is silently skipped. The original `elif s**-1 in images` branch, which handled this case, was removed. That makes the image wrong for any relator containing an inverse generator, so the homomorphism check will likely still fail or give wrong results.

The patch fixes IndexColumns but leaves the base Columns class untouched. The issue reports CREATE INDEX with '"name"DESC' for a plain descending index, which comes from Columns.__str__ (col + ' ' + suffix) in the original code. Looking at the upstream fix, Columns.__str__ was changed to add the suffix only when nonempty. If Columns in this repo version still does '{}{}'.format(quote_name(column), suffix), the plain case would still produce '"name"DESC'. Actually, in the Django version before the fix, Columns.col_str did `try: return self.quote_name(column) + self.col_suffixes[idx]`, so the DESC case gives '"name"DESC', and the upstream fix changed Columns to use ' {}'.format(suffix) if suffix. The patch doesn't touch it, so the main bug in the issue remains and hidden tests for Columns (e.g. test_descending_columns) would fail. Also it adds a stray reproduce script to the repo root.

The patch is hacky and likely wrong. The real fix changes Join.identity to include filtered_relation and equals() to compare full identity, whereas this patch also adds a string-replace hack in as_sql and rewrites the filtered relation condition in add_filtered_relation. That rewrite mutates children while iterating and replaces relation_name prefixes with the alias, which would break existing behaviour (e.g. condition lookups validated later, F() references, nested conditions as Q objects). The string replace of table_name with table_alias in compiled SQL is dangerous because it can corrupt SQL for the base table or the correct alias. It also adds a stray reproduce.py file. Existing filtered_relation tests would likely fail.

The patch fixes both Columns and IndexColumns to add a space before the suffix only when it is non-empty. This matches the upstream Django fix. However, it does not touch the places that pass col_suffixes with a leading space. In this Django version, the schema editor's _create_index_sql passes col_suffixes as ('DESC' or ''), and the previous code relied on ' DESC' being passed. Upstream changed the order strings in django/db/models/indexes.py from ' DESC' to 'DESC'. The issue example shows "name"DESC, so the suffix has no leading space here, and the patch is consistent with it. Other users such as the Postgres and MySQL schema editors, and the unique constraint code, pass suffixes only via Columns, so the fix covers them.

The patch swaps the align branches in _get_aligned_offsets, which matches the upstream matplotlib fix ("left"/"bottom" -> offsets = d; "right"/"top" -> height - h + d). VPacker uses the same function with left/right and is unaffected, because "left" and "right" are still mapped to the same branches as before. HPacker with top/bottom is now correct.

The visible patch consists only of committed build artifacts (_build/html/ files such as doctrees and .buildinfo), and the diff is truncated. No source change to sphinx/ext/autodoc is visible, so the inherited-attribute docstring lookup is not shown to be fixed. Adding generated build output to the repo is also undesirable.

The upstream fix is `if 'get_%s_display' % self.name not in cls.__dict__: setattr(...)`. This patch uses hasattr(cls, ...), which also matches inherited attributes. That breaks the abstract-base case: an abstract parent with a choices field gets get_foo_display set on it, and a child inheriting the field gets a copy of it, but hasattr finds the parent's partialmethod bound to the parent's field object. Likewise, a child that overrides the field with different choices would keep the parent's display method, which uses the parent's field and its choices. Existing tests such as model_fields test_choices/test_overriding_FIELD_display and tests for inherited choices overrides (e.g. test_field_name_clash or the 'foo_display' override with new choices in a child) would likely fail. Multi-table inheritance behaves the same way: the child doesn't re-contribute the parent's field, but a child redefining the field with new choices would fail. A concrete failing case is model_fields.tests.GetFieldDisplayTests.test_overriding_inherited_FIELD_display, which exists in the upstream change: a child overrides choices on an inherited field and expects the new choices to be used. With hasattr, the parent's partialmethod stays, so it would fail. The patch also adds stray repro files to the repo root.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix for this issue (ticket #28435-ish). In the single-instance fast-delete path, it sets the instance's pk attribute to None after deletion, which is exactly what the issue requests. The multi-instance fast-delete path goes through the later code, which already clears PKs for instances in self.data, so existing behaviour is unaffected.

The rewrite maps each relator's array_form symbols to domain generators via presentation generators and multiplies images**power, which is correct for PermutationGroup and matches the upstream fix. It also should work for FpGroup and FreeGroup domains, where domain.generators are the group's own generators and ext_rep[0] gives the symbol. One risk: for FpGroup, pres.generators are the FpGroup generators, whose ext_rep[0] is the symbol, and r.array_form symbols match. Images keyed by domain generators is consistent with how homomorphism() builds the dict, so behavior is preserved.

The upstream fix swaps the align mapping in HPacker: `hd_list = [(h, yd) ...]` was left alone and instead `align` handling changed: in matplotlib's fix (PR #24456), HPacker's align 'top'/'bottom' were swapped in _get_aligned_offsets (`if align in ['left','bottom']` -> `['left','top']`... actually they changed `elif align in ['right','top']` to bottom). This patch instead changes hd_list to (h, h - yd), which changes the descent semantics and offsets for children with nonzero ydescent, and doesn't swap top/bottom semantic. For DrawingArea with yd=0, hd becomes (h, h), so 'bottom'/'top' behavior with descent h would shift everything: for 'baseline' alignment this breaks results badly (descent h means baseline at the top). Also it adds a stray reproduce_bug.py file. Likely fails hidden tests.

The real fix in requests 2.27.1 was to stop mis-parsing proxy URLs in rebuild_proxies/resolve_proxies in sessions.py (Proxy-Authorization was stripped). This patch doesn't address that. It also adds an 'Authorization' header to proxy requests, which leaks proxy credentials to the destination server, a security regression. It also changes behavior for username-only proxies, which would now get no Proxy-Authorization header, and existing tests would likely fail.

The core change in options.py matches the upstream Django fix (kwargs.get('empty_label') or _('None') if blank else None), so the issue is resolved and the hidden tests should pass. The extra files (reproduce.py, test_settings.py, myapp/__init__.py) are clutter in the repo root, but they should not affect the tests.

The patch deviates from the upstream Django fix. Upstream, the non-filtered-relation branch keeps `j.equals(join)` and the filtered-relation branch uses `j.identity == join.identity`-style comparison (`equals(join, with_filtered_relation=False)` in newer versions). Here the patch changes the default branch from `j.equals(join)` to `j == join`. `Join.__eq__` compares full identity including filtered_relation, whereas `equals` ignores filtered_relation. That changes behaviour: normal joins would no longer reuse a filtered-relation join alias, and in the filtered branch `j.equals(join)` ignores the filtered_relation so different FilteredRelations on the same relation could still be merged, which is the bug in the issue. Reuse restricted to `can_reuse` might help in some cases, but the logic looks inverted relative to the upstream fix, so it likely breaks existing tests and may not fix the issue.

The upstream fix produces the message "TimeSeries object is invalid - expected ['time', 'flux'] as the first columns but found ['time']", and the hidden test likely matches that exact text via pytest.raises(match=...). This patch emits a different message ("missing required column: 'flux'"), so such a test would fail. The patch also makes unrelated changes: it pins setuptools in pyproject.toml and adds stray reproduction and test scripts to the repo root. The existing test for wrong first column ("expected 'time' as the first column but found 'banana'") would also break, since the missing-column message replaces it.

The patch removes the faulty PermutationGroup branch in _image, so s = r[i] and the lookup falls through to `s in images` or `s**-1 in images`. That fixes the inverted-generator case from the issue. The upstream fix did a similar simplification, rewriting _image to use the images of generators directly. But test_edge_cases.py includes a swapped-generators case that may not be a valid homomorphism, so it could raise. This is a standalone script, not part of the hidden tests. The main concern is whether r[i] for PermutationGroup is a generator, an inverse, or a FreeGroup symbol. In _check_homomorphism, domain.presentation() gives a FpGroup with free group generators, and `gens` are the presentation's generators. For permutation groups, `images` is keyed by domain generators, so r[i] (a free group element) would not be in images. The old code mapped r[i] to a domain generator via gens.index, but only when r[i] was in gens. The patch removes that mapping, so for permutation groups s stays a free group symbol and is not in images, which would break things. Looking at the code: in _check_homomorphism, `if isinstance(domain, PermutationGroup): gens = list(domain.generators)`? In that code `_image(r)` uses `images` built from `dict(zip(gens, images))` where gens are the presentation generators for non-permutation groups, but in the permutation case the presentation relators are in terms of the FpGroup symbols. If the original code mapped via `domain.generators[gens.index(r[i])]`, then `gens` is the presentation's generators and `domain.generators` the perm ones. Removing this mapping would make `s in images` fail for perm generators, then `s**-1 in images` also fails, leading to the else branch. This is likely to be broken, though the upstream fix was different, so it's uncertain.

This matches the upstream requests fix (PR #6028): prepend_scheme_if_needed now re-adds the auth to the netloc, which parse_url separates out. The surrounding code already assigns `auth` from parse_url, and the patch adds the netloc join after the swap, same as upstream. Proxy URLs with credentials keep their userinfo, so the 407 is fixed.

The fix in dates.py changes the condition from `level < 2` to `level == 0`, so the offset is shown for month-level ticks and the year appears. Upstream matplotlib made the same kind of change (the issue-fix removed the 'level < 2' check), and the logic after the loop for offset formats should handle level 1. However, the patch adds junk files (PNGs, repro scripts) to the repo root; these are clutter but do not affect the hidden tests. Existing tests with month-level ticks may have changed expected offsets, but upstream also changed those baselines, and the hidden tests likely reflect the new behavior. The upstream fix was `if level < 2: show_offset = False` -> removed entirely? Upstream: 'for level in range(5, -1, -1): if len(np.unique(tickdate[:, level])) > 1: if level < 2: show_offset = False; break' remained, and the fix changed the format of offsets in the zero_formats/offset_formats area... Uncertain. Upstream fix (PR #22206?) changed `if level < 2` to `if level == 0`, I believe, which matches this patch.

The real fix in requests 2.27.1 was in adapters.py: proxy_headers() calls get_auth_from_url and builds Proxy-Authorization, and the bug stemmed from rebuild_proxies in sessions.py / the handling of proxy URL credentials (a 407 on 3.8.12 came from urllib3/http.client tunnel header handling). Here the patch only adds a Proxy-Connection header in HTTPProxyAuth, which users don't use when credentials are in the proxy URL, so it does not address the issue. It also adds an unrelated header that could break existing tests expecting exact headers.

The upstream fix modifies Collector.delete() in deletion.py to set setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None) in the fast-delete path. This patch instead sets self.pk = None in Model.delete(), which covers the fast-delete path for the instance itself. In the normal path, Collector.delete() already sets pk to None for all collected instances, so this is redundant but harmless. Setting self.pk = None works for regular pk fields. For multi-table inheritance, the pk is the parent link (e.g., parent_ptr); setting self.pk = None sets the pk attname, which is fine. With keep_parents=True, the normal path doesn't clear parent pk... actually the collector sets the child's pk attribute only for its model's pk, and the child's pk is the parent_ptr_id, so the result is the same as self.pk = None. Hidden tests, such as test_fast_delete_instance_set_pk_none, would pass. Calling delete on an instance with a None pk is rejected earlier by the assertion. One edge case is that the collector's delete clears the pk of other instances in the fast-delete path, but only a single instance is involved here. Overall the patch looks correct.

The patch makes any join with a filtered_relation always create a new alias, but this breaks reuse of the same filtered relation alias across multiple setup_joins calls, such as in filter(), the select, and ordering. Join.__eq__ and equals() compare filtered_relation, so the reuse in Query.join (reuse_aliases) handles that case before calling table_alias. The actual Django fix changed Join.identity/equals and the alias lookup, and was more subtle. This patch looks too simple: in Query.join, the reuse check uses reuse_aliases with j.equals(join), and only if none matches does it call table_alias with create=True anyway. So table_alias with filtered_relation not None and create=False happens only in cases like the first join creation (alias_list empty) or reuse is not allowed. Cases where the base table is re-added with a filtered relation and no existing equal join would previously reuse alias_list[0], which was the bug. The patch fixes that. The risk is low, but the upstream fix was exactly the same: 'if not create and alias_list' changed to 'if not create and alias_list' with filtered_relation check? Upstream commit (#34362?) changed Join.identity to include filtered_relation and in table_alias... I recall the fix being in Join.equals, which ignores filtered_relation, and so on. Uncertain, but the patch is plausibly correct.

The patch changes the error message for any mismatch in the leading columns to a 'missing required column' message. If columns are all present but in the wrong order, missing_columns is empty and the message becomes "missing required column ''", which is wrong. It also breaks the existing message format that tests rely on. The upstream fix produces "expected 'time' as the first column but found 'time'" only in the mismatch case, and for a removed column gives "TimeSeries object is invalid - expected ['time', 'flux'] as the first columns but found ['time']". Existing tests such as test_required_columns check for "TimeSeries object is invalid - expected 'time' as the first column but found 'c'", which this patch would fail. Hidden tests would also check the upstream message, so this patch almost certainly fails.

The patch matches the fix proposed in the issue and the upstream Django fix: it keeps a user-supplied empty_label when the field is blank and falls back to _('None') otherwise. When the field is not blank, empty_label stays None, as before. The change is minimal and does not alter existing behaviour when no empty_label is passed.

The FutureWarning matches the issue's proposal, but the patch also pins setuptools==68.0.0 in pyproject.toml, which is an unrelated build change that could break the build or install. It also adds a stray reproduce.py to the repo root. Existing tests that add structured arrays to a Table may now fail because astropy's test config turns warnings into errors. The upstream fix also changed those tests and added a docs/changelog entry, and this patch does none of that.

This matches the upstream Sphinx fix (PR #7773 era) almost exactly: it removes the analyzer parameter and iterates the MRO, using each class's module analyzer to find attribute docs. The signature change could break callers passing analyzer, but the only in-tree caller is updated. Upstream made this same change, so hidden tests should pass.

This matches the upstream matplotlib fix (PR #22201). When level is 0 (years differ) the tick labels always show the year, and the check unique == 1 is not satisfied for years like 2021, so show_offset would stay True. That would be wrong. Upstream code is: `if level < 2: show_offset = False` changed to `if level < 2 and np.any(unique == 1)`? Looking at upstream: 'if len(unique) > 1: # if 1 is included in unique, the year is shown in ticks; if level < 2 and np.any(unique == 1): show_offset = False; break'. Yes, upstream has exactly this. For level 0 (years), unique years like 2021, 2022 do not include 1, so the offset would be shown, but upstream behaves the same, and the tests pass. For level 1 (months) with January in the range, the year appears in the tick label and the offset is hidden. Without January the offset is shown. Correct.

The patch keeps a caller-supplied empty_label when the field is blank and falls back to _('None') otherwise, which matches the upstream Django fix. For non-blank fields it still sets None, as before. The only difference from the issue's suggestion is that an explicitly passed empty falsy value (such as an empty string) is respected, which is arguably more correct.

The patch hardcodes URLs for only None and int, and pins dependency versions in setup.py, which is unrelated and harmful. It also changes merge_typehints to run in signature mode, where annotations are not recorded the same way, and it replaces return nodes with hardcoded links instead of cross-references. The upstream fix was to make None a pending_xref in the signature through type_to_xref in the python domain, so this patch would likely fail the hidden tests.

The patch rewrites Meta.ordering inside contribute_to_class, which runs before fields are added to the model, so self.get_field(related_field) will raise FieldDoesNotExist for any ordering containing '__pk'. It also mishandles ordering entries such as '-option__pk' (leading '-'), non-string expressions like F() or OrderBy (the `in` check fails on them), and descending prefixes. It does not fix the actual check in _check_ordering, which should accept 'pk' after a relation. The patch also mutates user-declared ordering and drops the trailing newline at end of file.

The patch sets show_offset = True when level < 2, which is already the default, so it changes nothing for the year-spanning case. It would make the offset show whenever ticks span multiple years or months, but the upstream fix is different. Upstream changed the condition: `if level < 2: show_offset = False` stays, but the offset formatting logic was changed so the year appears when January is absent from the ticks. Here the level<2 case (years or months differ) previously disabled the offset on purpose, because tick labels already show the year. Enabling it there would draw a redundant offset (e.g. the year) when ticks cross years, and would break existing tests that expect no offset in that situation. It also doesn't address the issue itself, where the ticks span months within one year (level 1), since labels like 'Mar', 'Apr' don't include the year and January is missing, so the year is shown only when a tick label is 'Jan' (which is replaced with the year). Setting show_offset True there would make the offset show the year, which might partly fix the issue, but it also affects the multi-year level 0 case, where the offset would be empty or wrong. Since the offset format for level 0 is '', the offset would be empty, and for level 1 the offset format is '%Y', so a year would show. But in cases where Jan labels already show the year, the offset would duplicate it, which fails existing tests.

The issue proposes a FutureWarning while keeping the NdarrayMixin behavior in this release, and only removing the clause in 5.2. The patch emits the warning but also immediately changes behavior to Column, which is the 5.2 change. Existing tests, such as test_ndarray_mixin, expect an NdarrayMixin and would break. The upstream fix kept the view as NdarrayMixin and added the warning.

The patch iterates over the whole MRO and calls dir(cls) for each class, which returns inherited names too. Since the first cls is subject, every name is already added with the subject's own handling. For later classes, unmangled names already in members are skipped, so the loop adds nothing new. The only difference is that names in obj_dict map to ClassAttribute(subject,...), but the original code did the same, and names not in obj_dict map to ClassAttribute(subject, ...) from the first pass only if cls is subject. In the first pass, names not in obj_dict now get ClassAttribute(cls=subject,...) rather than None, which changes the behavior. Because the class is set to subject for inherited names, the docstring lookup in the attribute getter uses (subject namespace, name), which is no better than before. The upstream fix did something different, changing the ObjectMember/analyzer lookup for inherited attributes with the analyzer's attr_docs. This patch marks inherited members as belonging to the subject, which breaks the inherited-members filtering that relies on the class being None or the base. It most likely causes failures in tests like test_autodoc_inherited_members and others, because inherited members get treated as the subject's own.

The patch misses two raise sites: in URLValidator, the UnicodeError handler for punycode (`raise ValidationError(self.message, code=self.code)`) is unchanged, so an invalid IDN domain gives no `value` param. The real fix covers it. A hidden test using `%(value)s` with an input that triggers that path would fail. Also, it adds a stray reproduce.py to the repo root, which is clutter, though harmless to tests. Other changes look right, but the URL case is a real gap against the issue's goal of including the value in built-in validators.

The patch swaps the alignment branches in _get_aligned_offsets so 'bottom' gives offsets of d (aligned at the bottom) and 'top' gives height - h + d. This matches the upstream matplotlib fix. For VPacker, which uses 'left' and 'right', the behavior is unchanged because those names stay in the same branches. Other usages with 'top'/'bottom' in HPacker are now correct.

The patch targets the wrong mode: the issue asks for None to be linked in signature mode, but this only changes description mode. It also likely breaks existing behaviour. In record_typehints, the annotation becomes ':obj:`None`', and that raw string is inserted into a paragraph node as plain text, so it renders literally rather than as a role. In modify_field_list, `annotation` is a local variable whose scope in that function is unclear, and the comparison to 'None' is probably never reached since the recorded value would already be ':obj:`None`'. The signature fix would need to go in sphinx/domains/python.py (type_to_xref handling None) or in the signature-building code, which this patch doesn't touch. Hidden tests probably check that the signature output has a pending_xref for None, which would fail.

This matches the upstream Sphinx fix, which changes make_xref in _parse_annotation to use reftype 'obj' for None. Intersphinx resolves None under py:data, and 'obj' maps to the data type, so the link resolves. Existing tests expecting reftype='class' for None would be updated by the hidden tests.
The patch matches the upstream astropy fix: the error message now lists all required columns and the actual leading columns, so it no longer says expected 'time' but found 'time'.

The patch adds params={'value': value} only to some validators. In URLValidator, the except block that catches ValidationError and retries with IDN handling still has `raise ValidationError(self.message, code=self.code)` without params, and the remaining validators (Min/Max value, length, decimal, file extension, etc.) are untouched. The upstream fix covered all of those, and hidden tests likely check that %(value)s works for them, e.g. in test_validators with custom messages for each validator. So the patch is incomplete and likely fails those tests.

The __reversed__ method returns reversed(self.dict), which works on Python 3.8+ where dict supports reversed(); Django at this version (the issue's fix) uses the same implementation. The extra scratch files in the repo root are clutter but do not affect hidden tests or behavior.
Adds __reversed__ returning an iterator over reversed list of dict keys, which works on all Python versions and matches the expected behavior; the only other change is a harmless leading blank line.

The patch removes the structured-ndarray to NdarrayMixin auto-conversion, so structured arrays now become Column. The upstream astropy fix (PR #13236) removed the same clause for 5.2, but also updated docs and tests and added a FutureWarning in an earlier version. With the clause gone, the later code path still handles structured ndarrays: `elif data_is_mixin` is skipped, and the ndarray falls to the Column creation branch, which should work for structured dtype. The NdarrayMixin import remains used elsewhere. Hidden tests likely check that structured arrays become Column, and this should pass. Remaining risk is from existing tests that expect NdarrayMixin, but those are updated upstream.

The rewrite of Add._eval_is_zero is risky: it calls expand(self) inside an assumption handler, which can recurse infinitely or be very slow. It also changes semantics. For instance, if all args are real and nonzero, the old code returned None when the terms could cancel, but the new code returns real_sum.is_zero and imag_sum.is_zero, which can return False when real_sum is a nonzero-looking Add that is actually zero. It also treats `imag_terms` and `real_terms` sums via self.func, which can recurse into the same Add logic. The extra reproduce script file is also committed. Overall it is likely to break existing tests or give wrong answers, and it differs from the upstream fix, which only returned None for im_or_z cases.

The patch changes both m12 and m21 to use a minus sign, but the standard rotation matrix has m12 = 2s(cd - ba) and m21 = 2s(cd + ba). With both entries negated, m21 is wrong, so the x-axis example would give [0, cos, -sin],[0, -sin, cos], which is still incorrect. The upstream fix changed only m12 to minus and left m21 as plus. The patch also adds stray reproduce and test files to the repo.

The patch mutates the user-supplied hyperparameter self.cv in fit, which violates the scikit-learn estimator contract and breaks clone and repeated fit. It also converts any cv splitter to a list in fit, so an int cv (5) is unaffected only because it lacks split and __iter__, while a splitter object like KFold gets replaced by a list. Splitters that need groups (e.g. LeaveOneGroupOut) would fail since it ignores groups. It manually loops over splits instead of using cross_val_score, which drops n_jobs parallelism and doesn't clone the estimator per fold. It also adds stray scripts to the repo root, and the upstream fix was simply to materialize cv via check_cv and pass it on. Hidden tests such as a check on parameter immutability or on KFold splitter use would likely fail.

The fix changes `self[i, j - pos - other.cols]` to `self[i, j - other.cols]`, which is the correct index mapping for columns after the inserted block. This matches the upstream sympy fix. The extra reproduce and test scripts at the repo root are clutter but harmless, since they are not collected as tests (reproduce_col_insert.py prints only, test_col_insert.py runs at import but is not in the test directory).

The standard rotation matrix has m12 = 2(cd - ba) and m21 = 2(cd + ba). The patch flips only m12 and leaves m21 as is, which gives the correct signs for the issue example (sin(x) in [2][1], -sin(x) in [1][2]). The row 0 entries (m01 = 2(bc - da), m02 = 2(bd + ca)) were already correct in the repo. The final hunk only touches the trailing newline or whitespace, which is harmless. This matches the upstream fix, which changed only m12.

This matches the upstream Django fix for the 'pk' ordering regression. Handling 'pk' via _meta.pk resolves the issue, and setting _cls = None for non-relation fields makes a following part raise AttributeError, which routes to the transform check, as intended. Before the fix, a later part such as 'field__lower' would still call get_field on the stale _cls; with _cls = None, get_field raises AttributeError, which is caught, and fld.get_transform(part) is then checked. The upstream fix is essentially identical.

The patch removes DecimalField.validate in forms/fields.py, which checked for non-finite values (NaN/Infinity) and raised 'invalid'. It moves that check into DecimalValidator, which now raises 'invalid' with code and params. But DecimalField only runs DecimalValidator if max_digits/decimal_places are set (validators added in models/forms). In forms.DecimalField, the validator is added only when max_digits or decimal_places is given. So a plain forms.DecimalField() would now accept NaN and Infinity, a regression; existing tests (test_decimalfield_support_nan/inf, e.g. test_decimalfield_1 or test_enter_a_number) would likely fail. Actually, the upstream Django fix for this issue did keep the validate method, so the removal is an unrelated and harmful change.

The patch only adds a length check in MutableDenseMatrix._new and never touches col_insert or its helper (_eval_col_insert), where the actual bug lives. The issue's wrong output would be unchanged. The extra validation could also raise errors in existing code paths, such as empty matrices.

The core fix matches the upstream Django change (content_type.save(using=db, update_fields={'model'})) and resolves the issue. The extra reproduce_error.py at the repo root is stray clutter, but it is not a test and is not collected by the test runner; it calls settings.configure at import time, which would only matter if something imported it.

The patch matches the fix suggested in the issue and the upstream Django fix: save() now receives using=db, so the content type is written to the same database as the surrounding atomic block. It changes nothing else, so existing behavior should be unaffected.

The patch allows arbitrary mul_symbol strings, falling back to the raw string, and for numbers it uses dot when the symbol is whitespace-like, else the symbol itself. This closely matches the upstream sympy fix (which used the same list and logic). The upstream test expects latex(3*x**2*y, mul_symbol='\\,') == '3\\,x^{2}\\,y' and for numbers latex(1.5e20*x, mul_symbol='\\,') == '1.5 \\cdot 10^{20}\\,x'. The patch allows arbitrary mul_symbol strings, and for custom symbols it uses the same value for both settings. In modify_field_list, the patch introduces `annotation = annotations['return']` but the original code at that point used `annotation` — in the original, the line `annotation = annotations['return']` was likely missing from the diff context, and the later code `nodes.paragraph('', annotation)` used a variable `annotation` leaked from the earlier loop (a bug). The patch maps Min() to -oo and Max() to oo, which is backwards: the issue asks for Min() = oo and Max() = -oo. It also puts the logic in Function.__new__ where Min/Max (a different class hierarchy, with its own ValueError in MinMaxBase.__new__) likely never reach it. The patch handles the 'all' and 'documented_params' targets, but the final else branch (target 'documented') still calls augment_descriptions_with_types with the original annotations, which may include 'return'. Within that function, 'return' is only added if the rtype is documented (force_rtype False), so the else branch is mostly fine. The upstream fix instead modified record_typehints to skip return annotations for classes (if objtype == 'class' pop it). The patch's ClassDocumenter change (show_return_annotation False) may suppress return annotations in signatures when typehints='description', which is already the default behavior because signatures drop annotations in description mode. The real issue is that record_typehints records the class's __init__ return annotation of None, and merge_typehints then adds 'rtype: None'. This patch removes it in merge_typehints for objtype 'class', which should work. However, the 'documented' branch may still add rtype if ':return:' is documented in the class docstring, which is an edge case. Also, passing show_return_annotation via kwargs in ClassDocumenter.format_signature is harmless. The hidden test likely checks the 'all' case with a class, and perhaps also with 'documented_params', and both seem handled. The risk is moderate: existing tests that expect return types for classes could break, but they are unlikely.

The patch adds an Enum branch to object_description, returning ClassName.member, which matches the upstream Sphinx fix. The patch replaces the `def _prepare_field_lists(self):` line with a new method, leaving the original docstring and body orphaned inside generate_foreign_key_dependencies (after the loop, as a dead string and subsequent code). `_prepare_field_lists` is no longer defined, so `_detect_changes` will raise AttributeError. The patch handles <, >, <=, >= via visit_Compare, but Eq (==) and Ne (!=) are not handled, which the upstream fix includes (Eq, Ne). The upstream Sphinx fix was in augment_descriptions_with_types/merge_typehints: it checks `if app.config.autodoc_typehints_description_target...` Actually the real fix (PR #10... ) was in record_typehints? Uncertain, but the patch is logically sound: classes have no meaningful return type. With autodoc_typehints='description' and autoclass_content, hidden tests expect no return field for classes, which this achieves. Risk: tests expecting rtype for class in other contexts is unlikely.

The patch only touches Relational.__new__ and Unequality.__new__ in relational.py, but the issue is about parse_expr(evaluate=False), which turns '1 < 2' into a Lt call via the AST transformer in sympy/parsing/sympy_parser.py. The patch fixes _print_Limit and _print_Relational so they respect printer settings, but the issue also says python(Eq(x, y)) should emit symbol definitions. With the patch, python(Eq(x, y)) would go through self._print(expr.lhs), which calls the PythonPrinter's _print_Symbol and records the symbols, so it would work. The existing test asserting 'e = Eq(x, y)' would need updating, and the hidden tests probably do that. The upstream fix did the same for Limit and Relational, and also changed some other places like the test files. Risk: the hidden tests may cover other printers or subexpressions that the patch doesn't touch, for example in the upstream commit, but those are probably limited to Eq and Limit.

The patch asserts real_apps is a set when not None, which matches the issue and the upstream fix (assert isinstance(real_apps, set)). One difference: an empty non-set value such as [] now fails the assert instead of falling back to set(). Upstream does the same, and all internal callers pass sets, so existing tests should pass.

The patch mirrors the upstream sympy fix (visit_Compare with a relational_operators mapping). It uses ast.NameConstant(value=False, ctx=ast.Load()). In Python 3.8+, NameConstant is a deprecated alias for Constant and accepts extra kwargs like ctx, so this works, but it was removed in 3.12 (the repo era supports older versions). Chained comparisons like 1<2<3 only handle the first op, which matches upstream. starargs/kwargs are ignored on newer Pythons. The upstream fix is essentially identical, so hidden tests should pass.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix: it asserts real_apps is a set when not None and defaults to an empty set otherwise. Adding __rand__ doesn't fix the issue: Q() & Exists(...) calls Q.__and__ first, which raises TypeError itself rather than returning NotImplemented, so Python never reaches Exists.__rand__ or Q.__rand__. Also, __rand__ on Q would only be invoked when the left operand is a non-Q, and it still calls _combine, which raises TypeError for non-Q. The real fix is in _combine, e.g. checking for conditional expressions or having Exists define a suitable path. The patch does not resolve the issue.

Removing the check alone likely does not return oo/-oo. With empty args, __new__ goes through _new_args_filter, then LatticeOp.__new__ builds frozenset(_args) and, if it is empty, returns cls.identity. The identity for Max is S.NegativeInfinity and for Min is S.Infinity, which is what the upstream fix relies on. Upstream sympy removed this same check and added the identity, which already existed (Max.identity = S.NegativeInfinity). In LatticeOp.__new__, args = frozenset(cls._new_args_filter(args)); if the set is empty it returns cls.identity. The remaining code in MinMaxBase.__new__ is: _new_args_filter, then 'args = frozenset(cls._new_args_filter(args))', then _collapse_arguments, then _find_localzeros, then 'if not args: return cls.identity'. So the patch should work. The upstream patch for this issue was exactly the removal of those lines, plus tests. The hidden tests probably check Min() == oo and Max() == -oo, and those should pass.

The patch routes subexpressions through self._print in StrPrinter, which matches the upstream fix for the issue (sympy PR #12900-ish). However, the issue also mentions python(Eq(x, y)) should emit symbol definitions; that is handled by the Relational change since the python printer's ReprPrinter/StrPrinter subclass then calls _print on Symbols, triggering _print_Symbol which adds symbols. The upstream test changes expected output accordingly. Risks: _print_Permutation changes use self._print on lists and ints, which are fine (_print_list gives '[1, 2]' same as str for ints; _print on int uses emptyPrinter -> str). _print(expr.func) for AppliedPredicate prints a Predicate via _print_Basic maybe producing different output than str(expr.func); e.g. Q.positive str is 'Q.positive', but _print_Basic would give 'Predicate(positive)'?? Upstream made the same change, so likely fine. _print(ring.domain) for domains: the domain is not a Basic; falls to emptyPrinter -> str, fine; but domain printers like _print_Domain? Upstream matches. Also the Limit dir print: _print of Symbol '+' prints '+', fine.

The patch changes _find_signature to return a list instead of a single tuple (or None), but does not update its callers. format_signature does `result = self._find_signature(); if result is not None: self.args, self.retann = result`, so unpacking an empty list would raise ValueError, and a list of tuples would unpack wrongly. The patch makes Add._eval_is_zero return None instead of False when imaginary terms are present and the real parts sum to zero. The patch makes the n_jobs=1 path generate the same seeds as the parallel path, which uses random_state.randint(np.iinfo(np.int32).max, size=n_init). Upstream scikit-learn fixed this the same way. Existing tests that depend on specific random results could shift, but upstream made the same change.

The core change matches the upstream Django fix (guarding MaxLengthValidator with a max_length None check) and should pass the hidden tests. The stray reproduce.py at the repo root is clutter but harmless to behavior and tests.

The patch makes the n_jobs=1 path draw n_init seeds up front from random_state and give each run its own RandomState, as the parallel path does. Results are now consistent between n_jobs=1 and n_jobs>1, so the patch should resolve the issue.

The str.py changes fix Eq and Limit for sympy_integers. The python() fix, however, is a hack: it calls doprint twice, and PythonPrinter.doprint depends on state. The upstream fix added _print_Relational to PythonPrinter or similar. Here, the first pass collects symbols, but the second pass also appends to the same symbols dict, so there is no harm there. But the real problem is that Eq(x, y) is printed via StrPrinter._print_Relational, which uses self._print(expr.lhs). PythonPrinter's _print_Symbol then adds the symbols, so the python output would work after the str.py change alone. The double pass is redundant and harmless. Remaining concerns: the existing test asserting 'e = Eq(x, y)' would be updated by the hidden tests. Other printers, such as _print_Relational in other str paths (Unequality, etc.), are handled by charmap. Other issues the upstream fix also covered, such as Sum, Subs, and Integral in str.py, may be tested in hidden tests, e.g. test_printing of sympy_integers for Subs, Sum, and others. Also the stray files edge_cases.py and reproduce_issue.py in the repo root are junk. The risk is moderate.

This matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #30535 area): add `dependencies` from `_get_dependencies_for_foreign_key(new_field)` to AlterField operations when the new field has a remote model. `dependencies` is initialized per loop iteration and passed to `add_operation`, which accepts a `dependencies` kwarg. The patch has multiple problems. Q._combine now handles Exists directly, so Q() & Exists never reaches __rand__, which makes that method dead code. It also gives wrong results for the empty-Q case: Q() & Exists(...) builds an object containing the empty Q and the Exists, whereas upstream returns a Q wrapping only the Exists via copy. The upstream fix is `if not(isinstance(other, Q) or getattr(other, 'conditional', False) is True): raise TypeError`, followed by the empty-Q handling, and also adds Combinable.__and__ handling. Hidden tests likely check `Q() & Exists(...)` equals `Exists(...)`-based Q structures. Also, `Q` is not imported in expressions.py, so if __rand__ were called it would raise NameError, and the patch adds stray reproduce/test files to the repo. Also, `obj.add(self, conn)` with an empty self may produce an odd tree structure, and the comparison with `Exists(...) & Q()` is inconsistent. Tests like `Q() & Exists(is_ceo)` comparing to `Exists(is_ceo)` as a filter condition would likely still work at query time, but `assertEqual(Q() & Exists(), Exists())` style tests would fail. In upstream, `Q() & Exists(...)` returns a Q whose result is compared with Q(Exists) after copying, and the patch's structure differs.

The patch bundles a huge amount of unrelated junk: _build artifacts, conf.py, minimal_conf.py, a doc/contents.rst edit pointing at ../test_doc, and setup.py dependency pins that change the project's requirements. The autodoc change also looks wrong. It only collects consecutive signature lines at the start of the first docstring block, and the multi-signature handling in format_signature is dubious. In the loop that collects signatures it does not stop at the first non-signature line, so later signature-like lines get matched too. It then removes lines only up to the first non-matching line. The upstream fix handles multiple signatures per docstring via _find_signature returning a tuple and format_signature joining them with newlines; this patch departs from that, and hidden tests may fail on the return type or on how the results are used. Subclasses of DocstringSignatureMixin that call _find_signature, such as DocstringStripSignatureMixin, expect a tuple result, and the new list return type breaks them. The setup.py and doc changes would also break the repo.

The patch matches the upstream Django fix for this ticket (#33333-ish): it only appends MaxLengthValidator when max_length is not None. This follows the BinaryField precedent. Fields with max_length=None fail the system check anyway, and behaviour is unchanged for valid max_length values.

This matches the upstream scikit-learn fix: seeds are generated up front from random_state for both the sequential and parallel paths, so results are consistent across n_jobs. kmeans_single accepts an integer seed because it calls check_random_state internally, and the _init_centroids call in _kmeans_single_lloyd/elkan handles that. The fix reverses the insertion loop so each leading free matrix is inserted at position 0 in reverse order, which yields the original order (free_pos[0] ends up first). This matches the upstream sympy fix. The trailing 'return t' diff is only a whitespace/newline change and does not affect behavior.

The patch quotes the qop value in the Authorization header as RFC 2617 requires (qop="auth"), which matches the upstream fix in requests. Existing tests only check for 'qop' presence or run against httpbin, so this should not break anything.

The patch only changes ConciseDateFormatter.__call__, but the issue concerns the default AutoDateFormatter, which is what the reproduction uses. The real fix modifies AutoDateFormatter.__call__ and the _wrap_in_tex handling, with changes to DateFormatter and related code. Wrapping the result in __call__ doesn't change the axis tick formatting that the issue reports. Also, format_ticks in ConciseDateFormatter is unchanged, so the main path still isn't fixed. The patch is very likely insufficient for the hidden tests.

The core change appends -X options from sys._xoptions to the child args, matching the upstream fix (which uses '-X%s' if value is True else '-X%s=%s'). The flaw is that sys._xoptions stores flags like 'utf8' as True, so this patch emits '-Xutf8=True'. That is invalid for utf8 (Python expects -X utf8=1 or -X utf8), and the child would likely fail or misbehave. Upstream tests expect '-Xutf8' for such flags, so hidden tests would fail. The patch also adds a lot of junk files (testproject, test_xoptions.py) to the repo.

The original code already had suppress_context handling, so the real bug was that frames' exc_cause was computed from the wrong exc_value after switching exceptions mid-loop (the variable updated only after the last tb). The patch refactors into per-exception frame generation, so each frame gets the right exc_cause. This matches the upstream Django fix (ticket #31... uses get_exception_traceback_frames). Behavior is preserved: the first popped exception uses self.tb if it is the only one, then others use __traceback__. The __traceback_hide__ handling uses continue with tb advancing inside the loop; I should check that the code between lines (not shown) does 'tb = tb.tb_next; continue' for hidden frames, which it does in the original. The generator form works with frames.extend. It matches upstream.

The original loop inserted each leading free index at position 0 in increasing order, which reversed them. The patch prepends free_pos[0:first_dum_pos] as a block, preserving order. free_pos is a list, so the list concatenation works, and resulting_indices holds lists of indices. This matches the upstream fix. The generator expression is evaluated immediately by list(), so there is no late-binding problem.

This matches the upstream matplotlib fix for the issue: braces around ':' and replacing spaces with '\;' in _wrap_in_tex. The upstream patch is nearly identical (it used `.replace(':', '{:}')` and `.replace(' ', r'\;')`). Hidden tests that check tex-wrapped date formatting should pass.

The patch adds -X options from sys._xoptions for CPython. Values in sys._xoptions are True for flags without '=' and strings otherwise, so the formatting matches the original options. The upstream fix is essentially identical (args.extend(f'-X{opt}' for opt in sys._xoptions)), with the same effect; tests expect e.g. '-Xutf8' and '-Xa=b'. The `value is True` check handles both cases correctly.

The patch removes quote escaping in _format_value (no more replace("'", "''")), so a value containing a single quote is written unescaped and produces invalid FITS. The parser also no longer unescapes '' to ', so values with quotes won't round-trip. The _format_value change also drops the 8-char minimum padding (f"'{value:8}'"), which breaks existing formatting such as 'abc     '. It also changes pyproject.toml and adds a stray reproduce_error.py. This will break many existing tests.
